function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

message.content:
Here are a few ways you can order a cake, depending on what you’re looking for: | Option | What it offers | How to get it | |--------|----------------|---------------| | **Local bakeries** | Fresh, custom‑made cakes, often with seasonal flavors and local ingredients. | Search “bakery near me” on Google Maps or Yelp, call or visit the shop, or use their website if they have online ordering. | | **Online cake delivery services** | Nationwide or regional delivery, often with a wide selection of ready‑made and custom cakes. | Examples:
• **Goldbelly** – delivers specialty cakes from famous bakeries across the U.S.
• **Etsy** – many independent bakers sell custom cakes that ship nationwide.
• **Amazon Fresh** – offers a selection of cakes from local vendors in some cities. | | **Grocery store chains** | Convenient, often affordable cakes that can be delivered or picked up. | Check the bakery section of stores like Walmart, Kroger, Safeway, or Target. Many have online ordering and curbside pickup. | | **Specialty dessert shops** | Gourmet or themed cakes (e.g., vegan, gluten‑free, keto). | Look for shops that specialize in dietary restrictions or unique themes. | | **Catering companies** | Full service for events, including cake design, delivery, and setup. | Ideal for weddings, corporate events, or large parties. | ### Quick steps to place an order 1. **Decide on the type of cake** (size, flavor, dietary needs, occasion). 2. **Choose a provider** from the table above based on your location and preferences. 3. **Visit the website or call** the bakery/store. Many sites let you customize the cake online (choose frosting, decorations, message). 4. **Provide delivery details** (address, time window, special instructions). 5. **Pay online** (most sites accept credit cards, PayPal, Apple Pay, etc.) or arrange payment at the store. 6. **Confirm the order** and keep the confirmation number handy. If you give me your city or zip code, I can look up specific bakeries or delivery services that operate in your area. Happy cake hunting!
message.reasoning: User asks: "where can i order cake?" They want suggestions for places to order cake. We can provide options: local bakeries, online cake delivery services, grocery stores, etc. Provide some general advice. No need to call external API. Just answer.
